doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Chico Hamilton's cello group as an accident
summary: Poston confirms the story that Fred Katz played piano parts on cello at the Strollers Club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So I had the opportunity to interview Chico Hamilton and Buddy Collette and I was struck by — they spoke about the classic Chico Hamilton group and the fact that it had the cello and the guitar and it had this different sound. And what they both said made it seem like that whole thing happened out of just circumstantial like there wasn’t enough
room for a piano, that — those kinds of things that are so logistical and look what they lead to.

Yeah. I mean that was, you know, according to everybody it was an accident. And that’s according to all of them: Chico, Buddy, Jim Hall, Fred Katz. I mean they all agreed that it all happened with Fred playing — you know Fred was a very accomplished cellist and I mean he looked like a cellist — I mean everything about Fred — and he was actually an anthropology professor.
That makes all kinds of sense.

You know flowing hair and you know — so Fred I mean he was a brilliant cello player and he would bring the cello to the Strollers Club in Long Beach and at the breaks he would play cello pieces. And then when the band got back on the bandstand Fred couldn’t get back to the piano ‘cause it was too crowded, and Chico said, “Just play the piano parts on the cello.” I know that all sounds too good to be true but they all agreed that that’s what happened. So you know — we know that’s what happened.
